proof.text: The map $F\to A$, $e_i\mapsto f_i$, kills every $f_ie_j-f_je_i$, so it induces $\mu:M_f\to A$ with image $J$. For $x\in Z_f(P)$, the map $F\to P$, $e_i\mapsto x_i$, kills the same relations and induces $\hat x$. Every element of $K_f$ is represented by $\sum_i a_i e_i$ with $\sum_i a_i f_i=0$. Consequently $x$ is admissible exactly when $\sum_i a_i x_i=0$ for every such relation among the $f_i$.

proof.text: For admissible $x$, the map $(p,a)\mapsto a\bmod J$ kills each generator $(x_i,-f_i)$ of $W_x$, hence gives $\pi_x$; it is surjective. If $[(p,a)]\in\ker\pi_x$, write $a=\sum_i b_i f_i$. Adding $\sum_i b_i(x_i,-f_i)$ shows $[(p,a)]=[(p+\sum_i b_i x_i,0)]$, so $\ker\pi_x=\operatorname{Im}\iota_x$. If $\iota_x(p)=0$, write $(p,0)=\sum_i b_i(x_i,-f_i)$; then $\sum_i b_i f_i=0$, and admissibility from step 1 gives $p=\sum_i b_i x_i=0$. Thus $\iota_x$ is injective and the sequence in (1) is exact.

proof.text: In the extension of (2), $q(f_ie)=f_i(1\bmod J)=0$, so exactness gives a unique $x_i\in P$ with $j(x_i)=f_ie$. Applying the injective $j$ to $f_ix_j-f_jx_i$ gives $f_if_je-f_jf_ie=0$, hence $x\in Z_f(P)$. If $\sum_i a_i f_i=0$, then $j(\sum_i a_i x_i)=(\sum_i a_i f_i)e=0$; injectivity of $j$ and step 1 show that $x$ is admissible.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EE (lemma-explicit-ext, line 24413), read on an extension class as in Homology, Section 010I (section-extensions, homology.tex line 1260)

proof.text: The map $h:P\oplus A\to E$, $(p,a)\mapsto j(p)+ae$, kills $(x_i,-f_i)$ because $j(x_i)=f_ie$; it therefore induces $\theta:E_f(P,x)\to E$. For $y\in E$, choose $a\in A$ representing $q(y)\in A/J$; then $y-ae\in\ker q=\operatorname{Im}j$, proving surjectivity. If $h(p,a)=0$, then $a\in J$; write $a=\sum_i b_i f_i$. Injectivity of $j$ gives $p=-\sum_i b_i x_i$, so $(p,a)=-\sum_i b_i(x_i,-f_i)\in W_x$, proving injectivity. The defining formulas give $\theta\iota_x=j$ and $q\theta=\pi_x$.

proof.text: For $x'_i=x_i-f_im$, one has $f_ix'_j-f_jx'_i=f_ix_j-f_jx_i=0$. For every relation $\sum_i a_i f_i=0$, also $\sum_i a_i x'_i=\sum_i a_i x_i-(\sum_i a_i f_i)m=0$, so step 1 makes $x'$ admissible. The map $h_m:P\oplus A\to P\oplus A$, $(p,a)\mapsto(p+am,a)$, sends each generator $(x_i,-f_i)$ of $W_x$ to $(x'_i,-f_i)$ of $W_{x'}$. Its inverse $h_{-m}$ sends each generator back. Thus $h_m$ induces the claimed isomorphism of quotients; its restriction to $(p,0)$ and its second coordinate show compatibility with $\iota$ and $\pi$.

lean.statement: theorem cyclic_extension_cocycle {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {P : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (f : Fin t → A) (J : Ideal A) (hJ : J = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (F : Type w) [AddCommGroup F] [Module A F] (e : Module.Basis (Fin t) A F) (W : Submodule A F) (hW : W = Submodule.span A (Set.range (fun ij : Fin t × Fin t => f ij.1 • e ij.2 - f ij.2 • e ij.1))) (μ : (F ⧸ W) →ₗ[A] A) (hμ : ∀ i, μ (W.mkQ (e i)) = f i) : let Z_f : Set (Fin t → P) := {x | ∀ i j, f i • x j = f j • x i} let admissible : (Fin t → P) → Prop := fun x => x ∈ Z_f ∧ ∃ xhat : (F ⧸ W) →ₗ[A] P, (∀ i, xhat (W.mkQ (e i)) = x i) ∧ ∀ k, k ∈ LinearMap.ker μ → xhat k = 0 let W_x : (Fin t → P) → Submodule A (P × A) := fun x => Submodule.span A (Set.range (fun i => (x i, -f i))) let E_f := fun x => (P × A) ⧸ W_x x let iota := fun x => (W_x x).mkQ.comp (LinearMap.inl A P A) ∃ pi : ∀ x, admissible x → E_f x →ₗ[A] A ⧸ J, (∀ x hx p a, pi x hx ((W_x x).mkQ (p, a)) = Ideal.Quotient.mk J a) ∧ (∀ x hx, Function.Injective (iota x) ∧ Function.Exact (iota x) (pi x hx) ∧ Function.Surjective (pi x hx)) ∧ (∀ (E : Type z) [AddCommGroup E] [Module A E] (j : P →ₗ[A] E) (q : E →ₗ[A] A ⧸ J), Function.Injective j → Function.Exact j q → Function.Surjective q → ∀ lift : E, q lift = Ideal.Quotient.mk J 1 → ∃ x : Fin t → P, (∀ i, j (x i) = f i • lift) ∧ (∀ y : Fin t → P, (∀ i, j (y i) = f i • lift) → y = x) ∧ x ∈ Z_f ∧ ∃ (hx : admissible x) (theta : E_f x ≃ₗ[A] E), (∀ p a, theta ((W_x x).mkQ (p, a)) = j p + a • lift) ∧ (∀ p, theta (iota x p) = j p) ∧ (∀ y, q (theta y) = pi x hx y)) ∧ (∀ x (hx : admissible x) (m : P), let x' := fun i => x i - f i • m ∃ (hx' : admissible x') (change_iso : E_f x ≃ₗ[A] E_f x'), (∀ p a, change_iso ((W_x x).mkQ (p, a)) = (W_x x').mkQ (p + a • m, a)) ∧ (∀ p, change_iso (iota x p) = iota x' p) ∧ (∀ y, pi x' hx' (change_iso y) = pi x hx y))
